Missing-Data

Source: vignettes/Missing-Data.Rmd
Missing-Data.Rmd

Setup

First, lets load the package:

library(bvarnet)

Data

Now, we can load the example data:

data(studentlife)

Missing Data in bvarnet

If we look at the subset of variables that we use in the Vignette("bvarnet") c(“anxious”, “calm”, “conventional”, “critical”, “dependable”), we see there is approximately 90%90\% of missing data:

sum(is.na(studentlife[c("anxious", "calm", "conventional", "critical", "dependable")])) / (5*nrow(studentlife))
#> [1] 0.8988494

Fitting the Model

We fit the model using the usual call

fit <- bvar(
  id_col = "id",
  time_col = "day",
  y_cols = c("anxious", "calm", "conventional", "critical", "dependable"),
  x_cols = NULL,
  re_cols = NULL,
  re_temporal = FALSE,
  K = 1,
  data = studentlife,
  family = c("ordinal"),
  priors = set_priors(),
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 1000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  seed = 1337
)

Missing Data Handling

Currently, bvarnet is handling missing data by restricting estimation to completem correctly soaced time-series. Before constructing lagged predictors, bvarnet applies listwise deletion at the measurement-occasion level. Within each subject, a row is removed if any selected outcome or covariate is missing. The subject is not removed completely simply because one or more measurement occasions are incomplete (complete-case analysis). Entirely absent time points and rows removed through listwise deletion can therefore create gaps in the remaining time series. After listwise deletion, the gaps are preserved rather than compressed. To illustrate this we have the following example: suppose complete observations are available at occasions 11, 22, 44, and 55. So the observation at occasion 33 is missing. A VAR(11) model uses the transitions 1→21 \rightarrow 2 and 4→54 \rightarrow 5. It does not treat 2→42 \rightarrow 4 as a one-step transition. Occasion 44 is therefore excluded as a response because occasion 33 is unavailable, but occasion 44’s observed outcomes can still predict occasion 55. Excluding an observation as a response therefore does not automatically remove it from subsequent lagged predictors. The scheduled occasion index must be integer-valued, with one unit representing one lag step. This index is supplied by time_col, or by beep_col when separate day/session labels are used. Original occasion numbers must be retained when measurements are missing. Listwise deletion is computationally simple, but it reduces the available sample size and can produce biased estimates when the retained observations differ systematically from the omitted observations. This procedure does not impute missing values or estimate relationships across incomplete lag windows. It reduces the information available for estimating both temporal and non-temporal parameters, and retaining correctly spaced transitions does not itself guarantee unbiased estimates. Results still depend on the missingness process and on how the retained observations differ from those omitted.

Model Output

We can print an overview of the the model we just fitted using the print(fit) functions:

print(fit)
#> BVAR Network fit
#> ======================================== 
#> Family:      ordinal
#> Outcomes (p): 5 
#> Lags (K):     1 
#> Fixed eff.:   0 
#> Observations: 67 
#> Rhat max:    1.001
#> Divergences: 0
#> Priors:       beta ~ Normal(0, 1), phi ~ Normal(0, 0.5), kappa ~ Normal(0, 2) (all defaults)
#> Total time:  1.8 sec
#> ========================================

Here we get information about the number of variables and lags, the number of observations and some first indications if the model did converge.

Practical implications

Only observations with a complete and correctly spaced lag window enter the likelihood. This preserves the intended timing of all retained lagged relationships, but it may substantially reduce the number of observations available for estimating both temporal and non-temporal parameters. This procedure does not impute missing values or recovers temporal information from incomplete lag windows. If listwise deletion is inappropriate for the missingness process, users should consider a suitable imputation procedure or an explicit model for the missing data.
